summary:
Finding by fdev (FS-GG/FS.GG.Coordination#1026 comment 6358900581, 2026-10-23), from a live re-read of the default-branch release workflows in all FS-GG repositories.

A nuget.org GitHub Trusted Publishing policy matches the owner, repository, workflow file name and, only when it is set, the environment. It has no ref or branch field; ADR-0013 records the same policy shape. So under any policy without an environment, a same-named workflow file on any branch that has id-token: write can mint a push key for every package the policy's glob allows. A '*' glob turns this into a second writer for unrelated IDs.

Branch rulesets do not close the gap:
- The Coordination main-protected ruleset covers only ~DEFAULT_BRANCH.
- Branch creation is open to the admins, and every fdev agent authenticates as the same admin account, so a creation ruleset would need that account in its bypass list.
- A branch copy has actually run under a release file name: run 37971715740 ran callable-cli-release-publish.yml on a push to a routine branch on 2026-10-09.

Disabling a workflow does fence it, because a disabled workflow is keyed by its path and the policy's file name equals that path.

Fence practice used for the FS.GG.Execution.* old writers:
1. Narrow each policy's glob to the IDs its producer actually owns.
2. Delete the policies of retired producers.
3. Do not let a dormant or fail-closed job keep a second glob alive. Add a temporary scoped policy as part of any later recovery admission instead.
4. Optionally, add a main-only environment to each policy and its job. This needs workflow changes in each repository.
Before relying on a single-writer claim, recursively check that no other repository contains the package projects.

At capture the fence was partial. Two workflows were disabled (.github release-telemetry-host.yml and Coordination callable-cli-release-publish-011.yml), and a personal-repository publish job is held behind an environment with required reviewers. The nuget.org UI narrowing pass listed in the comment is a user step and was still pending. Unproved: whether nuget.org matches a reusable-workflow call by job_workflow_ref. The narrowed-glob fence does not depend on it.

Limits: policy state, workflow enablement and ruleset membership are live facts; re-read them before relying on the fence. This grants no publication or policy change.
title: nuget.org Trusted Publishing policies have no branch field: without an environment, a same-named workflow on any branch can mint
